headline: DMP Commissioner warns firearms may be used to protect life and property
summary: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police chief has issued a stern warning regarding the use of force to maintain law and order.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner has warned that firearms may be used if necessary to protect lives and property.
This directive comes as part of the police force's effort to maintain security and prevent potential unrest in the capital city.
The Commissioner emphasized that the safety of citizens and the protection of assets remain the top priority for the law enforcement agency.
The warning serves as a notice to those who may attempt to disrupt public order or engage in violent activities.
The DMP is on high alert to ensure that the city remains stable and secure during this period of heightened tension.

headline_marked: [[Bangladesh-made jerseys reach FIFA World Cup]] via Cape Verde team
headline: Bangladesh-made jerseys reach FIFA World Cup via Cape Verde team
summary: The national team of Cape Verde wore kits produced in a Dhaka factory, highlighting the country's growing presence in the global sportswear market.
details: Bangladesh's garment industry has gained global visibility as the Cape Verde national team made its historic FIFA World Cup debut. The team's jerseys were produced at a Dhaka factory of Capelli Sport, a New York-based sportswear manufacturer.

Cape Verde captured headlines with a surprise goalless draw against tournament favorites Spain in their opening match. While the result was a sporting landmark for the African nation, it also showcased the manufacturing capabilities of Bangladesh.
The kits were made using fabric supplied by the South Korean company Yongan Corporation. This partnership underscores the integrated nature of the global apparel supply chain.

Although Bangladesh is not competing as a nation in the World Cup, its manufacturing sector continues to strengthen its international presence. The country has become a key supplier of sportswear for various international brands and football clubs.

This achievement reinforces Bangladesh's position in the value-added apparel export market, demonstrating that local factories can meet the high standards required for the world's biggest sporting events.
caption:
From Dhaka to the World Cup! 🇧🇩⚽

Bangladesh-made jerseys are now on the global stage.

Bangladesh's garment industry has gained global visibility as the Cape Verde national team made its historic FIFA World Cup debut. The team's jerseys were produced at a Dhaka factory of Capelli Sport, a New York-based sportswear manufacturer.

Cape Verde captured headlines with a surprise goalless draw against tournament favorites Spain in their opening match. While the result was a sporting landmark for the African nation, it also showcased the manufacturing capabilities of Bangladesh.

The kits were made using fabric supplied by the South Korean company Yongan Corporation. This partnership underscores the integrated nature of the global apparel supply chain.

Although Bangladesh is not competing as a nation in the World Cup, its manufacturing sector continues to strengthen its international presence. The country has become a key supplier of sportswear for various international brands and football clubs.

This achievement reinforces Bangladesh's position in the value-added apparel export market, demonstrating that local factories can meet the high standards required for the world's biggest sporting events.
